sources.sections_read: Unprivileged Containers and Removing all Privilege

sources.limits: Its documented unprivileged-launch helpers do not require adopting a rootless kubelet; pod-wide coordination and disjoint allocation still need separate design. sources.title: NsJail configurable UID/GID maps and capability retention
sources.confirmed: NsJail exposes separate UID and GID range mappings, a user namespace, capability retention controls, and seccomp policy.
sources.limits: It is a process-isolation tool rather than a pod runtime; allocation, namespace sharing, and lifecycle integration must be added. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C02.json.

sources.title: OCI runtime-spec Linux namespace and ID-mapping configuration
sources.confirmed: OCI specifies user namespaces, uidMappings/gidMappings entries with containerID, hostID and size, and advises against changing referenced filesystem ownership to implement mappings.
sources.limits: The orchestrator must allocate and manage nonoverlapping ranges; OCI leaves those policies outside this schema and cautions against changing referenced filesystem ownership. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C02.json.

sources.title: Sysbox user-namespace isolation and exclusive-mapping design
sources.sections_read: User Namespace ID Mapping; Common vs Exclusive Userns ID Mappings; Process Capabilities
sources.confirmed: Sysbox documents paired UID/GID mappings, common mappings in CE versus exclusive ranges in EE, configurable exhaustion behavior, and capabilities confined by user namespaces.
sources.limits: The opened guide assigns common mappings to CE and exclusive mappings to EE; exhaustion may reuse ranges unless configured to fail, and mounted files require ID-mapped mounts or shiftfs. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C02.json.

sources.title: Linux user namespaces: identity maps and namespace-owned capabilities
sources.version_or_date: Linux man-pages 6.19, manual date 2026-02-08, HTML retrieved from tarball 2026-09-09
sources.sections_read: Description; Capabilities; effect on other namespaces; file access; colophon
sources.confirmed: User namespaces isolate IDs and capabilities; the manual explains capability checks against owning user namespaces and mapped-file permissions.
sources.limits: Shared-kernel vulnerabilities remain; file access depends on mapped identities, and namespace ownership matters. The opened manual is later evidence. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C02.json.

sources.title: gVisor application-kernel isolation
sources.sections_read: What is gVisor? and Why does gVisor exist?
sources.confirmed: gVisor provides a userspace application kernel with an OCI runsc runtime and reduces application exposure to the host kernel.
sources.limits: It does not itself specify the requested pod UID/GID allocation policy; workload compatibility and performance would require evaluation. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/B/C02.json.

sources.title: Podman automatic UID/GID ranges and explicit rootful mappings
sources.confirmed: Version 4.3 documentation contains automatic unique UID/GID ranges, direct mappings for privileged callers, and the restriction against per-container UID maps when joining a pod.
sources.limits: A subordinate-ID pool must be configured, volume ownership needs handling, and mappings cannot be set per container when joining a pod.
